utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-01-48-T, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Before we hear the witness, are there anything that the parties would like to say at this stage? Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No. Your Honour, the only matter I mention is that I'm going to ask the witness some questions about Zenica. And I should indicate that there's a transcript and there's a video recording of the Zenica transcript which has been given to the audiovisual people, and we have made a transcript of the relevant parts which -- if the witness -- depending on how the cross-examination goes, that may happen. I just mention that's a forthcoming possibility. He may just simply answer the questions without out it, so it might go be quicker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I hope so. And generally speaking, we give the equal time to direct and cross-examination of the witness. I hope during the weekend you have already gone over with all your questions. So I hope we could have this witness back home today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, it -- I'm not optimistic about it. We have, I can indicate, worked very late on the weekend on this particular witness, and we're going to endeavour to go as quickly as we can with him. But as will be seen, the Prosecution has put a large chunk of its case, particularly the de jure case through this witness, and it -- he really has to be given -- Your Honour will have noticed I haven't attempted to interrupt him very much or to cut him off, and because it's technical evidence in some ways, it sometimes takes longer and I can trial him less distributively because he has to be given a chance. So yes. But in any event, I will certainly attempt to comply with what Your Honour says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Did you have a good rest during the weekend?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By your leave, Your Honour, I would like to ask counsel for the Defence something, by your leave, before we begin. It refers to the further course of today's work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You mean the scheduling issues?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. My question is of an administrative nature. It has to do with some of the documents being shown to me. By your leave, Your Honour. If not, it doesn't matter so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, are there any problem with the documents that the counsel has shown to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have certain reserves with respect to certain documents, reservations, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that we will let the Defence counsel to start his cross-examination. Maybe those documents will be used in the future proceedings. If not and if you believe there's something very important, I believe that the parties will ask you some further questions. The Judges will ask you some questions on this respect. And at last you'll have a chance to make a statement on certain matters, at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no problem, Your Honour. I certainly wish to say what I have to say, and I thought it might be better to say it at the beginning rather than at the end. However, if I do get an opportunity to say it, then I will take the opportunity whenever you so decide. I am ready to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let's continue the cross-examination. Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Morrissey: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gusic. Mr. Gusic, we had finished on last Friday night with evidence about the IKM and how such locations are administered. I now want to take you to another topic, and it's one raised by the learned Prosecutor with you in evidence in chief, and that is the topic of investigations of breaches of military discipline and how and under what rules such breaches are dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, could the witness please have displayed to him the Rules on Military Discipline, which are MFI107.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, do you have in front of you those rules?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Would you please look at Article 2 of those rules. Does Article 2 describe what military discipline is?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. I'll just have a look. Yes, it's all right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, is that correct? Article 2 in brief summarises --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, would you go, please, to Article 5. Does that provide that for criminal offences or misdemeanours servicemen shall be accountable with the -- in accordance with the regulations regulating criminal offences or the regulations regulating misdemeanours in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina? Is that what it provides?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you look, please, at Article 6, which provides: "The accountability of a serviceman for an offence or misdemeanour does not exclude his being held accountable for an offence of a breach of military discipline too according to these rules" -- sorry, if according to these rules such offences constitute a breach of military discipline."

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, could the following page please be shown.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do have the following page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, you have the advantage over me because unfortunately I do not. Would you just excuse me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, on my screen at the moment the following page is not displayed, and the Prosecutor are in the same situation. Now we have it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you have a look now, please, at Roman numeral II, and under that the heading "Article 7." Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Negligent attitude"? Do you mean that? "Negligence in respect of property entrusted to his care," or do you mean the entire Article 7?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, I meant the entire Article 7.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I want to put questions about the entire Article 7. Does that list the type of military breaches to be dealt with under this set of rules, from Article -- from subarticle 1 right through to subarticle number 13?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see 17. I see up to 13.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if I said "17", I'm sorry. I meant to say "13," but ...

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From 1 to 13. Does that list the disciplinary offences that are to be dealt with under this code?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, could we, please, go now over to the next page, both in English and B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, while that's being done, can I just indicate my gratitude to the court staff who are performing this function. In preparing cross-examination, we sometimes have to jump from page to page, and we simply haven't had time to specify the correct computer number for each page. Therefore, there may be a little bit of inelegant jumping of this nature, and we appreciate the efforts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Gusic, do you now have in front of you - if you'd just excuse me a moment.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Which article?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I really -- the article I really wanted was 11 -- sorry, I've jumped over one. But just on this article -- on this page, would you look at Article 18, and then we'll jump back to the one I missed. So look at Article 18, please. Now, does Article 18 provide: "If an action during which a criminal offence or infraction has been committed also involves the commission of a disciplinary infraction, the serviceman may also be held accountable before a disciplinary court for a disciplinary infraction if so required by the special interests of the service."

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here. And then it also says that: "The proceedings before -- are before the disciplinary court shall be conducted independently from and irrespective of the outcome of the proceedings for the criminal offence or misdemeanour."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please look at Article 19. Does Article 19 provide for certain time limits governing the commencement of proceedings under these rules?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, could we please return to the previous page, and I want to show the witness Articles 11 to 13. Thank you. Okay. Mr. Gusic, would you just look, please, at Article number 11.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does that provide that -- for -- sorry, perhaps I should ask you this: You see the term "errors of discipline" and "disciplinary infractions" being used there?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does Article 11 pick up another piece of legislation which provides for the actual sanctions to be imposed?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A decree law is mentioned, the decree law on service in the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly. Does Article -- Article 12 deal with one of those sanctions, namely, the loss of seniority for a particular soldier who is the subject of these disciplinary proceedings?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does Article 13 disclose in the first paragraph that: "In some circumstances, the tribunal" -- or sorry, the military court can actually impose a disciplinary sentence of imprisonment of up to 60 days if none of the lesser punishments are? Just read it to yourself and then tell me if I've summarised it accurately.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes. Yes. That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that the position is that under this code, there is a grade -- that's perhaps not the right term. There's a sliding scale of potential punishments available to deal with military infractions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if the lesser or less serious sanctions are not appropriate, a sentence of up to 60 days of imprisonment can be imposed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now we need to go forward a number of pages to find Articles 67 and 70. And I request the assistance, if I may, of the court staff to help to find those because we don't have a page number for them. But it's Article 67 that is being sought. Thank you. Mr. Gusic, do you have in front of you under Roman numeral V the short Article 67?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... provide that: "The provisions of these rules shall be applied accordingly in a state of war provided that as a rule in a state of war no measures are pronounced whose execution, given the conditions and circumstances under which they are to be carried out, is inapplicable or impossible."

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that section give to commanders a realistic discretion as to how to deal with disciplinary offences committed in a time of war?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They have that right both in peace and in war. It's not just in war. It's their duty and responsibility both in war and in peace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just talking about -- sorry. Stop for a moment, please. I'm just talking about what's said in Article 67 itself, Mr. Gusic, where it refers to a state of war. Do you agree with the proposition I put to you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm telling you now, this is applied in war but also in peace. And it refers not just to commanders but to commanding officers at all levels who have subordinates. They're all duty-bound to implement this if under the rules there are people whom they can hold responsible, whom they have control over. So this refers to commanders at all levels who have subordinates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Would you go, please, to Article 70. And this is the last of the articles I'll take you to before some questions. Would you just read Article 70. I'll read it with you: "If it's impossible for the execution of a disciplinary measure or punishment to start within seven days of the day of its communication, its execution shall as a rule not be proceeded with. The disciplinary measures of confinement to barracks and soldier's detention and a disciplinary custodial sentence shall be executed only in conditions of accommodation in a barracks and if their execution does not expose the serviceman concerned to greater danger from war operations relative to the other members of the unit or establishment. The disciplinary measure of soldier's detention and the disciplinary personality of imprisonment shall be suspended or postponed also if this is required by the official needs of the unit or establishment or for the reasons of security and protection of persons referred to in paragraph 2 of this Article."

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And once again, that gives the commanding officer a discretion as to whether and how to proceed with disciplinary measures; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Gusic, did the -- I shouldn't ask you what happened in the briefing session, but what I'll -- well, I won't ask you about that. Instead, I'm going to put this to you: You don't deal with 30 murders of civilians, if it be 30 murders, or 15 murders of civilians if it be 15 murders, or even five murders of civilians, if it be five murders, under the military discipline code but you deal with it under the Criminal Code; correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You deal with it under both.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't investigate these matters of significant killings of civilians under the limitations of this code with its three-day limits, its seven-day limits, and its 60-day maximum punishments, do you, Mr. Gusic?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On Friday or on Thursday I think I was asked a similar question, not the same, however. It's correct. You have taken me through the articles of these rules, and from what we saw today, we saw that two parallel proceedings can be conducted: Disciplinary proceedings and criminal proceedings. The role of the commander in both proceedings is not the same. The criminal proceedings are to be conducted by a trained professional and the commander enables he professional to do so, while disciplinary proceedings are conducted by the commander. The two are not mutually exclusive. The conducting of criminal proceedings is independent from disciplinary proceedings. There are no limitations to criminal proceedings, but there are limitations to disciplinary proceedings and those are conducted exclusively by the commander, who is the superior of the person who has committed a misdemeanour or a breach of discipline. That is how I see it, at least. So the two are not mutually exclusive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I just want to move now to another document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's -- I'm grateful for that document. The next document I'd ask that the witness be shown is Defence document 65 ter 186. It's DD00.0836, and it's ultimately to be marked as MFI136.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, while that's being brought up on the screen, Mr. Gusic, I want to put to you that under the criminal procedure code, a part of which you're going to be shown in a minute, there are certain duties that are enjoined upon all citizens to respond to crimes and in particular crimes of a serious nature. But even before I et to that -- that document, do you agree that that's the case, that under the criminal procedures all citizens, whether soldiers or not, have got a duty to respond to crimes by advising relevant persons?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... that have got a particular competence have got further duties to actually investigate such crimes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall the details at present, but the essence of what you say is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, we'll come to the specifics.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I ask perhaps -- that if the court staff could assist me again, as I often ask, to go to page 3 of that document -- or the third page of that document. Not page 3 but the third page. We don't have that in English as yet, Your Honour. Now we do. Your Honour, could I just indicate that it seems that there is a delay of about 15 seconds between the -- perhaps the B/C/S going and the -- and the English going, and I sometimes jump the gun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, do you have in front of you there Article 148 of the Criminal Procedure Code?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And does 148(1) provide -- sorry, 148(2) provide that: "Working people in state organs, organisations of associated labour and other self-managing organisations and communities must report crimes" -- sorry, I withdraw that question. I've misled you. Would you mind just reading that -- reading that section to yourself.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine. I've read the first article.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Well, 148 is -- now, do you agree that that article captures some, if not all, of the -- of the duties that a citizen has to report crimes?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the state organs, organisations of associated labour and other self-managing organisations have the obligation to report the crimes to be prosecuted ex officio. Therefore, they are not talking about the working people but, rather, the official organs and organisations. As for the second paragraph, that's where it says "the working people in the state organs, organisations of associated labour and other self-managing organisation have the obligation to report the crimes damaging, prejudicing the socially owned assets or abusing the official line of duty." So they're not talking about the working people in general but, rather, about the organs, the organs of associated labour and self-managing organisations, and that's a different matter. These are not working people and citizens, as is usually phrased in such articles. And then in that case it refers to all the citizens across the board. Here, however, they only refer to the official organs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But would you now look to the following article, that's Article 149. Now, what obligation do you -- do you think that imposes or did you -- what obligation do you understand that to impose?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This article provides for the obligation -- I can't read the word at the end of the second paragraph. "In order to exercise the social self-protection, the citizens" - and then I can't read the following word - "to report the crimes" -- can you please help me just with this one word because this isn't really -- it's a very poor copy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, my apologies for providing a poor copy. Could I just give you what the English translation is at this stage, and if there be any dispute about its accuracy, the Prosecutor can take the point. Article 149 - and this is the English translation - provides in subparagraph (1): "For the sake of social self-protection protection, citizens ought to report crimes that are prosecuted ex officio."

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what do you understand to be the obligation arising from that provision?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This means that all the citizens who learn of a crime that is to be prosecuted ex officio should report one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Now would you go over to Article --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And could I ask that the court staff assist once again to go to the following page, and in particular Article 151. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, have you in front of you now Article 151?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not yet. Now I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Would you read Article 151. And in order to assist, I'll read with you, the first paragraph. Article 151(1): "If there are reasonable grounds to suspect that a crime prosecuted ex officio has been committed, internal affairs organs must take necessary measures to find the perpetrator of the crime, ensure that the perpetrator or accomplice do not go into hiding or flee, find and secure the traces of the crime and objects that might be used in evidence, as well as gather all information that might be of use to the successful conduct of criminal proceedings."

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, does that appear to you to authorise - I'm just trying to find the right phrase there, if you'd excuse me a moment - internal affairs organs to investigate crimes in a proper way. And, in fact -- I take that back. Does that appear to you not merely to authorise but to oblige internal affairs organs to conduct appropriate investigations into crimes?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. But it does not exclude the role and the duties of the army. However, you are right; they do have the obligation to act ex officio. However, as I've said, this does not exclude the role of the army if the perpetrator is a member of the army to conduct its own investigations and prosecutions. So this is not solely the obligation of the MUP but, rather, of the army as well. Whereas, if the perpetrator is a member of the army, then the MUP can perhaps initiate some actions in relation to the perpetrator, but in essence my answer to your question is yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I tender -- I offer for tender that document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Gusic, you know of a body called the SVB, which is the military security organ of the army; correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the SVB operate according to a set of rules; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now we have finished with the Criminal Code document and I now ask that the witness be shown Defence document 190(a). It is DD00.0903. It is to be marked for Exhibit 137. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, would you just identify whether or not the document in front of you is the Rules for the Military Security Service in the Armed Forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the cover page that I see, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now I'd ask the court staff's assistance once again. I wish to show the witness Rules 40 and 41 of this document.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read the text that I see here on the screen. I am -- I'm not sure if this is the entire article -- Rule 41.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, it's clearly not the entire article, but I'll just ask you to read Rule 40 and I'll read with you and then we'll go to the next page. Does -- first of all, I'd ask you to note that this is under a heading "The Military Security Service in criminal proceedings." That's Roman numeral V. And does it provide -- perhaps to be complete, I'll ask you to look at 39. Does it provide that the work and powers of the internal affairs organs as laid down by the -- I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the internal affairs -- oh, yes, yes. Yes. You're reading Rule 39 now?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry. Perhaps I didn't make myself clear, Mr. Gusic. I'm reading Article 39. I'll read it with you.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These fine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... "...the Internal Affairs organs as laid down by the ZKP relate also to the conduct of an action taken by authorised officers of the Military Security Service in pre-trial and criminal proceedings within the frame of their competence." Now, you notice that?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... and that is the SVB, the military security, jurisdiction to do the same job in relation to the crimes in the military that the MUP, the MUP internal organs, do in relation to crimes in civilian life; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That -- that is why I've stated a moment ago that one does not exclude the other. I was unable to invoke the specific rule, but you're right, yes. The -- under the law, this organ is vested with the power to conduct these proceedings. However, once again, this does not exclude the possibility for trained professionals and organs to be hired. It does vest this body with the power of conducting the proceedings, but also if it proves to be unable to conduct those, it provides for the possibility for someone else to take over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, we're going to come in a minute to the ability of the military security forces to share responsibility with other organs. At the moment, what I'm seeking to do is to establish beyond any doubt that the military security forces have got competence, and in order to do that I want to take you through these. I appreciate it's a -- a slow process, but it has to be done. Would you please go to Article 40.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I -- while Mr. Gusic is reading that, can I just indicate that in the B/C/S version Mr. Gusic has the whole paragraph on one page. But the Court and counsel do not, so that I would ask that now the court staff turn over the page to allow the English speakers or English readers to observe how Article 40 finishes.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Article 40 -- well, perhaps I'll ask you -- I'll ask you to read Article 41 before I put the general questions to you. So Article 41 provide -- and, Mr. Gusic, while you're reading Article 41 could you indicate, please, when you get to the end of the text so -- and then ask the court staff to turn over the page for you and they'll do that. But I'll read with you: "On the basis of the information gathered, officers of the Military Security Service in the command of the brigade or corresponding or a higher ranking officer in the Military Security Service shall submit a criminal report to the competent military prosecutor's office. In cases where it's necessary to carry out certain investigative actions immediately, an authorised officer of the Military Security Service shall immediately inform the competent military prosecutor" -- and there is more there to which you may refer if you feel that it's important to do so. So in order to satisfy yourself, please read the whole paragraph, although I'm not going to question you about the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pursuant to Articles 40 and 41, is it the case that military security goes through a process when investigating a crime committed within the military, the process being to commence the investigation, to gather material, and then to approach an investigating judge or investigating prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's one course of action. But they can at the same time conduct the proceedings jointly. Although, what you've said is correct. And unless they can get a military prosecutor to appear for an on-site investigation on the ground, then they do it themselves. Because this part has to do with the submission of a criminal complaint -- report only, and this report has to be supported by certain evidence, which means that the investigating judge wasn't -- didn't go up there on the ground. If the investigating judge is there on the ground, then the paper they would produce would be produced jointly. This, of course, if a -- if magistrating -- if an investigating judge is available. And when I say "available," I mean of course keeping the specific wartime circumstances in mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. In addition to those matters which you've raised, it's apparent, isn't it, that on the face of those provisions there is no time limit governing when the Military Security Service must contact the military prosecutor or investigative judge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for the criminal proceedings. But again, as I say, this does not exclude the conducting of a disciplinary proceeding, because we have rules that allow for both proceedings to be commenced on the basis of one and the same criminal act or act.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Gusic, before I come to that -- that dual approach, could I just conclude by asking you this: Military Security Service being competent -- sorry, that question is badly phrased. I withdraw it and I'll start again. Although the Military Security Service is plainly competent to investigate crimes committed within the military, you would agree that they are entitled to work together with civilian organs in investigating such a crime, particularly when the victims of the crime are civilians; do you agree?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it that an example of that process is the case that you referred to which occurred later on, that being the case in Fojnica involving the killing of the monks.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that what you'd say is that it's -- where military personnel kill civilians or where it's possible that they have done so, the Military Security Service is plainly competent but you would say the civilian police services are also competent; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In cooperation. They -- one does not exclude the other. They are not mutually exclusive. They have the same common goal, and of course the task will be taken over by the side that is more competent, more professional, and of course the goal is the same, to investigate the crime and punish the perpetrators thereof.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. All right. Now,--

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just excuse me one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Gusic. Sometimes we have to decide whether to put a particular document at this stage, and we're not going to put that yet. Mr. Gusic, on Thursday last week the learned Prosecutor took you through the provisions of the military discipline regime, but as you will recall did not take you through this procedure; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. He didn't show me those, but what he did show me was correct; the procedure as shown to me at the time, and as we went through it together, shows a disciplinary procedure as was applicable and what you've been showing me today is also true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, do you know what the murderer Enes Sakrak was sentenced to when he pleaded guilty to killing a small -- a small child and that small child's mother? Do you know what sentence he got?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must admit that I don't. I've never had occasion to hear what the sentence was. I just know that it was a high one, a very high one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you don't get confined to barracks for 30 days or demoted from a position of seniority for murdering civilians, do you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not the perpetrator himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But those who brought this about of course should be held accountable, because after all it was a heinous crime. And this sort of a sentence -- an appropriate sentence cannot be rendered for the perpetrator within the military. It has to be dealt with by a court, because this is definitely under aggravated crime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Gusic, it's quite obvious, isn't it, that the pre-eminent investigation into the incident at Grabovica had to be a criminal investigation by the SVB and possibly civilian police as well and not a disciplinary breach investigation; do you agree?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do 99 per cent agree with you, but the perpetrators themselves should -- would definitely not be punished under a disciplinary procedure. There has to be a criminal proceeding instituted, although there could have been a sort of a disciplinary procedure conducted at the same time for some minor breach that was related to this crime. But definitely the perpetrator of the crime should have been prosecuted, meaning that there would be investigations and prosecutions both by the civilian MUP and by the military prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, you've already indicated that -- on Thursday, when you gave your evidence in chief, that this military security way of investigating a crime was not the subject of evidence. And what I want to ask you is this: Did you point out to the Prosecution that in tendering the evidence about disciplinary procedures, that that was capable of creating a highly misleading impression as to the course that the investigation should have taken?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not quite sure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: -- what counsel is really getting to. Would he please put his question as -- is he talking about counsel during proofing and is it an appropriate line of questioning, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Morrissey, maybe you could rephrase your question, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, could I seek to justify the current question in this way: That Your Honour will have seen that on Thursday you were presented with evidence about the military discipline process, and in particular focus was laid upon the time limits that were included in that; namely, a three-day time limit for commencing operations, and so on. And that could have only been led, given the case against Mr. Halilovic and the relevance of the evidence, it could have only been led for one reason, that reason being that Halilovic failed to comply and that he didn't do so. Now, we are very concerned to make sure that the Court is -- that's the reason why I've gone in the detail I have here. In my submission, it goes to the credibility of this witness. And I want to put it as to the credibility of this witness, rather than making a derogatory comment at a later time without giving him the opportunity. I want to put it to him and ask him whether he was prepared to be part of putting what he must have known to be a very lopsided and misleading picture to this Tribunal. I want to put that to him to give him the chance whether to agree or to rebut it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well -- well, Mr. Morrissey, I believe that you have the full right to attack the credibility of this witness because you are doing the cross-examination, and you have already made your point very clear from the transcript. But there's no need to lead this witness to attack the other party, that is, the Prosecution, so that's why I asked you to rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Your Honour, I've had my try at justifying the question, and I'm not going to try again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, finally, could I ask you the question directly then and not involve the -- the Prosecutor in any way: Why didn't you point out to this Court at the time when you were being led slowly and surely through the military discipline rules that the truth is this should have been investigated by military security according to the proper rules? Why didn't you point that out?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It isn't true that we never said that. We just didn't go into detail. I don't remember now, but you showed me the article this morning. We did say that for the crimes committed, proceedings are to be commenced under the Criminal Code of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which has to do with your question. You -- you have gone through this piece of legislation with me this morning, and the OTP decided not to. But had they done so, they would have reached the same conclusions. I tried to be brief and answer specific questions. It isn't true that we never said that criminal proceedings can be instituted, because the Prosecutor also invoked the Article 3 or 4 - I'm not sure - providing for the institution of a criminal proceeding in Bosnia and Herzegovina for the commission of crimes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: May I offer for tender MFI -- I'm not sure if I offered 136 already. But if I didn't, I offer MFI136 and MFI137 for tender. Perhaps in order to allay the Prosecutor's concerns, by the previous question I want to make it clear that it was to this witness's credit that the -- that the question was going. Because I can understand sensitivity by the Prosecutor about being attacked sideways. So I make it clear that's what the -- that's what the -- what the questions were all about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, thank you. That completes the questions on that topic for now. And we are going to return later on to how the investigation itself actually unfolded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Would you just excuse me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: My apologies. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I now wish -- Mr. Gusic, yesterday -- sorry, on Friday I promised a chronological approach, which has not in fact happened. I commenced to take you to some of the conclusions at the Zenica conference, and we went through a great deal of the Zenica material. And after that, you may recall His Honour asked a question about forward command posts, and we then proceeded to analyse forward command posts for a period of time. And this morning we've now covered military security in the abstract. I now wish to return, if I may, to the chronology, dealing with Zenica. Now, Mr. Gusic, you have already indicated that to your knowledge those proceedings were videotaped; correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you've already indicated too that you've seen that videotape some several months ago; correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the tape but the DVD. It was shown to me in Sarajevo a few months ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly. Now, Mr. Gusic, a transcript has been prepared, and I'm going to have that transcript shown to you, and I'll make a couple of explanations about that transcript before we do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But could --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm instructed now that there's been a technical hitch with that -- with the text of that document. What I propose to do is to put some propositions to the witness, and it may be that if he -- if he adopts those, there'll be no need to -- to go to that -- that extent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, I'm going to put some passages of the Zenica discussions to you. If you dispute the authenticity of what's being put or if you think it's being taken out of context, you feel free to make that comment because the transcript can be made available to you and indeed, if needs be, the tape can be made available to you. Okay? Now, first of all, I'm going to put to you something said by Mr. Halilovic, the accused man. And when I say "mister," could I just ask you this: You refer to him frequently as General Halilovic. The fact is that at no time while he was on active service in the Bosnian army was he called "General Halilovic"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. But for me he was and will remain a general.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gusic. Anyway, I want to put to you something said by Mr. Halilovic on this tape, and this is early on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a passage that's a reasonably lengthy one, ten lines or so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "The goals of the war, meaning the division of the country. In favour of division or against it, I believe that this is the crucial issue Dedo, if I am not off target, I actually -- I just want to share my opinion with you. And there's room for each of us to reach our own conclusion since we do not have a final answer to this question. According to information from the press, the Presidency in its full composition without Ganic has made a decision in Geneva to embark on such a division which is being done now. My opinion in this regard is that we should not dwell on this issue for too long for the simple reason that the aggressor's goals are to destroy the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina and to destroy the Bosniak Muslim people. Because of that, even through these talks, negotiations, they will offer a part of the territory, exactly as much territory as would constitute the defeat of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina if this share of the territory is accepted, and that would mean a shameful defeat for the army and primarily for the Bosniak Muslim people. In my view, this would be the first step on the way towards our final destruction. Our task is as follows: To reinforce the army, to step up combat readiness, to get stronger." Now, Mr. Gusic, I don't expect you to remember in your own mind everything that was said by Sefer Halilovic, but broadly speaking, do you accept that he said those words at the Zenica conference? And we can show you the tape, if needs be.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there's no need. I cannot assert that every word is correct, but yes, I think this is the essence of what he said -- or rather, part of what he said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you're quite correct. It is only part. And I'm just going to put parts of what everyone says to you. But from that passage, it's quite evident to you that a couple of -- I want to put a couple of points to you about that passage. The first one is that the meeting at Zenica took place during a political debate in Bosnia, the debate being whether Bosnia ought to accept the partition of Bosnia into different ethnic cantons or whether a unified multicultural Bosnian state ought to be persisted with. Do you recall that debate existing at around this time?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I have to say quite sincerely that I never wished to express my views on such issues because I felt they did not belong to the military domain, but yes, such discussions were conducted at that meeting as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, I can assure you I am not going to seek to paint you into any political position or to delve into your political views. Do you understand that? I'm asking you to comment simply upon what was said. All right. Well, you agree there that in a very brief way Sefer Halilovic was putting the position against the partition of Bosnia; correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I now want to take you to something said by Vahid Karavelic, the commander of the 1st Corps. And I'm going to read this to you. Well, perhaps I'll -- I'll ask you a general question. Vahid Karavelic as commander of the 1st Corps was always concerned that Sarajevo, which was in his zone of responsibility, be very heavily protected by troops; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Any commander would want that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was his duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course. And what I want to read you is a -- a passage from Karavelic at that meeting, and he says this: "In the zone of responsibility of the 1st Corps, there are Chetnik troops." I interrupt now. I'm just -- I'm going over a part that's lengthy and irrelevant. But he then says: "4.000 to 5.000 troops have left the Igman front with at least 3.000 to 4.000 pieces. That is why I had to pull out a strong company from each of the brigades in Sarajevo in order to close the lines, consolidate the defence, and that is why Sarajevo as such is getting to be somewhat vulnerable." Now, do you accept that Vahid Karavelic said those words at Zenica?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to comment on the correctness of this information, but I think this is what he said -- or rather, that was the context in which he spoke, among other things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Gusic, at the moment I'm just asking you to confirm the facts and I'm not asking you to look into Mr. Karavelic's mind. Okay? Now, I've got some questions about the speech made by Arif Pasalic, the commander of the 1st -- of the 4th Corps, who had the responsibility for Mostar. Did he say this -- sorry, did he in general speak about the activities of the HVO in his area of operations?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In particular, did he say - and I'm quoting now - "The recent goal of the aggressor, particularly of the extreme part of the HVO, recently has been to destroy the ABiH forces, that is, the 4th Corps in the Dreznica-Blagaj area." Do you accept -- do you accept that he said that at the Zenica meeting?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he did. I don't want to have the transcript shown, but I think the essence is what you said, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, as I've said, at any time you're concerned, you can ask for the transcript. Now, I've got some other questions about Mr. Pasalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And could I indicate perhaps for the benefit of the witness, the Court, and the Prosecutor that some of these questions will get answers that are irrelevant elsewhere to other witnesses and some of them don't fit into the narrative in a very attractive way. But some of it is in the narrative and what's coming now is in the narrative.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, by way of background to the next set of questions, I just want to ask you some general questions. I understand your sensitivities about commenting on other army officers, but unfortunately in this Tribunal you're a witness rather than a military man, and to the extent that the questions are relevant, you're going to have to answer them. There was some tension between yourself and Arif Pasalic concerning the role of and the zone of operation of your 6th Corps, which was a new corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say there was tension, but perhaps our opinions differed, in view of certain units. And I responded to those issues at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, to which I'll take you. Mr. Gusic, did Mr. Pasalic at the Zenica meeting say this: "In cooperation with the forces of the 6th Corps and other units which are deployed in the territory of the 6th Corps, there is a realistic possibility for active combat activities towards Raska Gora, that is, Vrdi, or from the direction of Dreznica, Vrdi, Raska Gora, Goranci, with a view to liberating the road, which I consider the lifeline. In our view, if Mostar is not opened towards Jablanica and if the road is not opened by the beginning of the autumn rains and winter, we will find ourselves in very dire straits. We as well down there in the zone of the -- of responsibility of the corps will be in a very, very difficult situation for the ABiH units in the north, that is, for the 6th Corps and others." Then a little bit further down the page, he says this - and for the Prosecution's sake, if they want to check it, it's about 13 lines down the page - "We have food for five to seven days. I've already informed you of that. The war hospital is in an extremely difficult situation. I believe this will improve with the arrival of the team you've dispatched; however, three elements are important, in that we are lacking -- three elements are important: Anaesthetics, sterile dressings, and blood, i.e., plasma." Now, do you recall -- well, do you accept that Mr. Pasalic said that at the Zenica meeting?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the context in which he spoke, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I want to put another passage to you here. And this is the comment perhaps that you were referring to earlier: "The division of 4th Corps and its forces, that is, the establishment of the 6th Corps, was wrong in my mind." Now, do you recall Mr. Pasalic giving that opinion at Zenica?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He probably did, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally for Mr. Pasalic, did he say this: "You have to deal with my problem of food urgently, within three to five days. If this humanitarian convoy does not enter, we now have only one meal a day. If the convoy does not enter, people will have nothing to eat. This is final." Did Mr. Pasalic say that?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to now take you to some things that you said at this meeting. And this is referring now to the problems between the 6th Corps and the 4th corps. Did you say: "The problem with the 4th Corps is the problem of various missionaries in the territory of Jablanica, Neretvica who are trying with using all sorts of means to return one part of the units onto the strengths of the 4th Corps even as we speak." Now, did you make that comment and that complaint at Zenica?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. But with respect to this comment - and when I heard the tape, I said the same thing - I think that there was a comment by the late General Pasalic just before I spoke referring to part of the units located in that area, which he referred to as "paramilitary," and that's what I was responding to actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. So what you say is you were talk about paramilitary units there. Well, did you --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not I, but General Pasalic. And I said to him that he was referring to these units as "paramilitary units," and now he wanted them to be part of the 4th Corps. So that's what I was talking about. The units he was referring to, he himself had referred to as "paramilitary units" just before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, did you go on to say this: "They are trying -- they have tried in the 44th Brigade with the brigade commander. He immediately informed me of their arrival. They did not have any success with him. Now they are targeting the battalion and company commanders. I believe that this has a major impact on the mood of the soldiers in the 44th Brigade, as the Ustasha forces are now trying to regain lost territories around Pisvija." [phoen] Now, did you go on to say that?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that context, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's not paramilitary, is it? That's the 44th Brigade, which was the Jablanica Brigade under the command of Kovacevic, which was part and parcel of your 4th Corps and no paramilitary unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I said, and the late General Pasalic referred to the 44th, the 45th, the Zulfikar Detachments, and the other units there that he contacted as "paramilitary units," and he even called the military police battalion a paramilitary unit, and my response was actually a response to what he said, and I probably read out what I said verbatim. But I was referring to my own units, which were within the composition of my corps, and to this very day I think that they were regular units and not paramilitary units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly. Mr. Gusic, did you go on to make this -- did you then give some details about an attack on Makljen? I'll read you a passage and then I'll ask you the question. Question: "If the 317th" -- sorry, not question. This is a passage here. "If the 317th Brigade which, according to some organisational order, belongs in the strength of the 6th Corps managed to do its job, Operations Group West, even at one moment yesterday evening when I was with its commander, he told me our target is Makljen, I agree. Our target is Makljen. We could have already been on Makljen if the decision had not been changed." Now, Mr. Gusic, I'm not asking you about the -- why things happened like that, but do you agree that at Zenica you spoke about a 6th Corps operation in the direction of Makljen?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you read this passage again. If you do, you will see that it wasn't I who spoke about this but the commander of OG West, and I asked whether this brigade was on my strength, if it -- and it was. Makljen, its true, was a very important facility, and it's a good thing that we managed to take it and control it. But this was done by OG West, including the 317th Brigade without my knowledge; although, they were part of my organic composition. And that's what I was talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the point is, what I'm getting at here, that there was an operation by 6th Corps units at that time towards Makljen; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The units of the OG West, yes. But the units of the 6th Corps, no. The 317th Brigade was engaged without my knowledge, although it was part of the 6th Corps. And that's the reason for my reaction. I said that if it belonged to the 6th Corps establishment-wise, and I agreed that Makljen was a good target, but I should have been informed. I should have known about this, and I might have been able to assist. And those may not be the words I used, but that's what I meant to say. Who recruited my unit and why and what for; that's what my question was about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just point on that map that's behind you to your right the direction in which an attack from the Bosnian army positions towards Makljen -- in fact, I'll rephrase the question. Just listen to the question and then you can stand up and do. Just point on that map to the direction of the attack that is referred to in the discussion I've just read out to you.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you asked me about just now, I can say now that I don't know. I was not involved. But I can show you the direction I was talking about. I am not certain what the exact direction of attack was. I know as much as you know about it from the transcript. But these are these two axes, the two directions, here and here, one and two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd just ask you to confirm this: Those two axes that you've just pointed out on the Neretva 93 map -- sorry, the two -- the two directions that you've just pointed out on that map correspond, do they not, to the arrows ultimately drawn on that map by those who drafted it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd like to see anyone draw them differently. That's what the terrain makes possible. Any other way of drawing those lines would be unrealistic. You wouldn't be able to defend such axes. These were the two best axes that existed, and anyone with any knowledge of the terrain and of the course of combat operations would have chosen the same directions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But, Mr. Gusic, what I'm putting to you is this: By the time the Neretva 93 map came to be drafted some 10 to 14 days later, whenever it was, the directions that it proposed were directions that the 6th Corps unit, 317th Brigade was already pursuing; do you agree or disagree?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are the only two possible axes, the only two realistic axes, the ones offered by the terrain. How can I not agree that this was underway when I was asking why the brigade had gone in that direction? It had gone as part of Operative Group West, yes. And if you wanted to do something similar today, you would use the same two axes again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Last question about Zenica: Did Bakir Alispahic, the Minister for the Interior, appear there and did he say, "I think that this area of Herzegovina is very unstable and that at the moment we all need to help, for I am afraid that we are going to fail the test on the subject of Mostar, Jablanica, and Konjic. I shan't meddle in combat tactics with your military evaluations, but I think it would be wise to freeze all fronts and move the combat operations down there." Did Mr. Alispahic say that or do you accept that he said that at Zenica?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On Thursday, when I enumerated the participants in the meeting, I wasn't sure whether Minister Alispahic had been there or not. But now, when you showed me the list and when I saw the list of participants, I think he was there. With respect to what he said, what I can recall is that he did say something. I have no reason to doubt that what you've read out is correct. It's probably what you read out, because where else could you have got this but from the transcript or from the video recording that I myself saw? So yes, that's probably correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, bearing in mind that you'd actually seen this video yourself some months ago, can I ask you, then, what is the reason for not mentioning this to Alispahic?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't sure -- I simply wasn't sure whether he was there or not. I am sure I recognised him on the video recording when I saw it in Sarajevo, and if I saw the recording today, I would recognise him again. But there was no special reason for me to recall his presence. I was focussing on the military men there. Maybe that's why.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Bakir Alispahic a powerful figure politically in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that, but I do know he was a minister and that ministers have a great deal of authority. So he was probably one of the more influential people in that period of time, because he was a minister, a minister of the interior, in fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, you indicated in your evidence in chief to the Prosecutor that you were given three directions by Rasim Delic as a result of the Zenica meeting. This is at page 56 of the transcript, Your Honours, 56, line 24. Did you say this: "The 6th Corps were given three axes along which it was supposed to carry out." In paragraph 3: "The reassigned to the 6th Corps T-boundary between the 3rd and the 6th Corps being -- this is the axis towards Prozor. The second one" -- I won't -- I'll stop. I won't read the whole thing. Can I just put to you that there was three directions that were specified: Prozor, Kiseljak, and Mostar? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And there was another task in connection with fortifying the lines reached in the direction of Igman, Bjelasnica, Visocica, but no active combat activities were required there. And along the three axes that you mentioned, active combat activities were required. That's why I spoke about three directions, because that's where active operations were needed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I now want to take you to the week after Zenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Morrissey, you know, since we have finished the -- the Zenica conference, I believe that it's quite time for us to take a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can imagine it's high time. I agree it's high time. Can I just indicate that went slower than I anticipated, so I'm going to reorganise things a little bit here, because that was -- that was slow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let's take a little bit longer break. We'll resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll have our next break at 15 minutes past 12.00 or 20 minutes past 12.00. It depends on how it goes. Yes, you may proceed, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, what's coming now, so that the questions are clear, I'm going to ask you some questions about the week that follows Zenica. I'm then going to ask you some questions about the role of Chief of Staff, deputy commander, and senior person on the terrain. And you'll recall the Prosecutor asked you questions about that. I'm going to press you about that. After that, you'll be asked some questions about the order by Rasim Delic of the 30th of August, which you've already commented on to some degree with the Prosecutor. After that, you'll be asked some questions about the arrival of the inspection team and what they did early in September. And after that, we'll come to the visit on the 4th of September of Rasim Delic and then on to the meeting at Dobro Polje on the 5th of September. So that's where the direction of questions is going, for your benefit. After the meeting at Zenica, did you meet with Vahid Karavelic, Sefer Halilovic, and Sevko Hodzic at the front of your command post in Konjic on the 22nd of August?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not outside the command's post, but we did meet in Konjic. It wasn't outside the command post though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command post was situated in the town itself and was exposed to firing from the positions, so that we met outside the army command post of the former JNA. And Karavelic spent the night in Konjic at the time when we met.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that time, it was discussed that the 6th Corps was going to conduct operations towards Vrdi and towards Makljen; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We commented on all the three axes assigned to the 6th Corps: The Mostar, Prozor, and Kiseljak axes. And we did not attach particular importance to any one of these three.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, two days later, on the 24th of August, did you receive an order from Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And I'm going to ask that the witness be shown this document. This is Defence document 198. It is DD00.1036. And it's to be Marked for Identification 138.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have that document in front of you now, Mr. Gusic?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, in the future, it might help when -- when the document comes up onto your screen, if you wouldn't mind just indicating to us. That would help. Now, would you just look --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- at the address. Is that -- at the start of the letter, does that appear to be a document that's addressed to the command of the 6th Corps?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the form, is it an order?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for their information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes. Would you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the court staff please assist by turning this over to the second page of this order. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have that second page? Sorry, pardon me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that a command from -- sorry, an order from you -- from Sefer Halilovic directed to you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, although that's in the form of an order, that was -- Sefer Halilovic in his capacity as Chief of Staff had no power to command you at that time, did he?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He could if so authorised by the commander and if acting as his substitute.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And perhaps picking up from that answer, the truth is that a Chief of Staff is not structurally speaking in the -- in the line of command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the Chief of Staff, but a deputy commander, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But I'm not asking about deputy commanders right now. I'm asking --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Chief of Staff, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, a Chief of Staff can issue orders if specifically authorised by an order of a superior; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's in that capacity that you tasked your own Chief of Staff on another occasion to perform command functions at an IKM at Fojnica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. All right. Well, yes, well, I offer that document for tender. Mr. Gusic, you did receive that document, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, could I next ask that Mr. Gusic be shown, please, another document. Okay. Now, we've just got to find the proper number for this, Mr. Gusic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this is an order from Commander Delic to you dated the 26th of August, and that is Defence document D12, and its number is DD00.0050, and it's to be MFI139.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do have the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, sometimes there's a temporary mix.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic is that correct an order from Commander Delic to you dated the 26th of August?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in that order, does he direct you -- look at -- look at paragraph number 1 of that order, please.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does he direct you to engage your forces to help the defenders of Mostar in a particular direction, that being the direction of Vrdi village?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Using the pointer, would you please indicate on the map that's just to your right there what the line of advance was.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the line of advance but the line of attack that was assigned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I accept your correction, Mr. Gusic. But you've just -- anyway, you've appointed the line of attack assigned there, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you agree with me that it's the line of attack that ultimately happened in Neretva 93, the operation?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the line of attack requested by Arif Pasalic, and as I've shown on the map here, this is one of the axes along which Neretva 93 took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Would you please look to paragraph number 4 in that order, and could you observe there that attacks are ordered in the area of responsibility of the 44th and 45th Mountain Brigades? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just point on the map there that's behind you whereabouts the 44th and 45th Mountain Brigades are located. Start with the 45th and then go to the 44th.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay -- which one. Point to the 45th. Just point to the 45th, if you don't mind.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you point to the area of responsibility of the 44th.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And it's just so that later on the Court can understand where these units were base. The 45th Brigade was under the command of a individual named Haso Hakalovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Haso Hakalovic's unit was sometimes known as the Neretvica Unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Neretvica Brigade, I believe it was called. It was in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And it's the fact also that some units from the Neretvica Brigade played a part in Neretva 93; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the 44th Brigade was based right in the town of Jablanica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But answering to your earlier question, the 44th Brigade Battalion was engaged along this axis up here, because the -- one of the battalions -- battalion commanders of the 44th Brigade -- that is, the 45th Brigade got killed up there. So the battalion commander of the 45th Brigade was killed in Neretva 93 operation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I just put to you that the name of that person was Padalovc; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seid Padalovc, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, that happens later on when Neretva 93 is actually occurring; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this stage, we are still in August, and in fact in particular on the 26th of August. Other questions about the 44th Brigade: The commander of that brigade was Enes Zukanovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, paragraph 4 urges engagement by the 44th and 45th Brigades; correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, Commander Delic was asking you to get the 44th and 45th Brigades into battle to help Mostar at that time; correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to introduce the brigades into action. They are asking for combat actions, that is, active defence actions, which means that I was not ordered to engage the entire brigade but to, rather, take positions opposite the enemy along those axes in order to create conditions for combat action to be taken along the assigned axes. Therefore, active combat actions, yes, but for defence purposes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, could I suggest to you that it was for a little bit more than that. And we'll see if you agree with this. Part of the strategy in this order here, the order of the 26th, was that there would be attacks at Makljen, at the top, Vrdi, at the bottom, and you would engage the 44th and the 45th in the middle in order to keep the HVO busy and prevent them from reinforcing the areas attacked. Now, is that accurate or inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
