utterances.text: I cannot agree with you when you say that this was an operation taking place at the time. At the time, it was merely an activity. I don't know what the commander's idea was at that particular point in time, but I can offer my comments as to what his reasoning was at the time, but I cannot claim that this was really the case. He perhaps wanted to deceive the enemy -- or rather, conceal the actual line of attack. But it is true when you're mentioning this particular zone that the -- in the entire sector there were active combat actions but not in the form of an operation, especially when we are talking about the central part, where the 44th and the 45th Brigades were engaged. It was just a smaller portion of their units engaged with the aim of deceiving the enemy as to what was in reality going on in the -- on the ground. The aim of the action was to link up Mostar with a part of the Jablanica area. Therefore, it wasn't really an operation; it was a limited action with the forces that we had at our disposal. Later on it turned out that these forces by themselves were insufficient.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, it does -- you can comment on this, whether it's accurate or not, but it does rather appear that the 6th Corps was engaging on all of the lines which Neretva 93 ultimately adopted in that last week. Now, do you agree or disagree with that proposition?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're looking at a part of the zone of the 6th Corps, and I can tell you that at the same time on that same day - please allow me to finish - there were combat activities in the area of Kiseljak, therefore -- throughout the zone of responsibility. Therefore, I cannot say that what you are saying is true. It was just a part of the zone of responsibility throughout which there were combat activities. But it is true that there were combat activities taking place along these lines that you're interested in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But they were of a limited scope.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But so far as the areas shown on that map are concerned, it remains the case that what ultimately was drafted on the Neretva 93 map was in all its essentials already part of the 6th Corps' plans and already part of the 6th Corps' actual operations. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already told you this once this morning, that these were the only possible axes to be taken. Other justifiable axes do not exist. They are the only ones along which the forces can advance and can be expected to perform successfully. If today you or somebody else were in position to conduct such an action, you would opt for these axes because they are determined by the configuration of the terrain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, I'm going to show you another document now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is the first blatant treachery against the e-court system by the Defence. In this case, we have only recently had this translated, and we are going to have to do it by paper. What we are planning to do is to upload it as soon as we can. But could the witness please be shown document D311.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And I think this will be MFI140.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You haven't been given that yet. Sorry, might I ask the court -- sorry. Pardon me. Could the court usher please give that to ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, would you -- you may take as much time to read this as you wish. I'm just going to direct you to some formal details of it before anything else happens. Could you look firstly at -- at its address, and do you agree that it's addressed to the 6th Corps command personally to the commander?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I understand you haven't read the -- the text as yet, so I'll -- I'll delay those questions. Would you look to the final page, please, and look to see that it's signed by a member of ONO -- I don't know whether they're the right letters, but by a man called Enes Zukanovic.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you read it, can you just tell us who Enes Zukanovic was.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Enes Zukanovic was an officer from the operations and training unit. He basically dealt with intelligence. He was an officer of the Yugoslav People's Army who was also an officer in the army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And for the most part he performed duties of an intelligence officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've mentioned he was an intelligence officer. He was an intelligence officer attached to the staff of the 6th Corps; is that the position?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wasn't an assistant of mine but was an intelligence officer within the intelligence organ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of which corps?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 6th Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So this is a document from somebody -- from Mr. Zukanovic within the 6th Corps to you. Now, would you just take the time to look at that document, please. And then I'm going to ask you some questions about it. And just to be sure, while you're reading it, I'm just say something to you about the questions I'm going to ask. There are no tricky questions about this. I'm simply going to ask you to confirm certain of the details in there, and perhaps ask you to point them on the map. Now, as you read, are you in a position yet to agree that this is a proposal that particular -- it's nothing more than a proposal, but it is a proposal that particular attacks be carried out by three specified units of the 6th Corps?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those units are the Prozor Independent Battalion, the 45th Brigade, and the 44th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've already shown the Tribunal members where the 44th Brigade and the 45th Brigade are. Could you mind just breaking off your reading for one second and point on the map to the position where the Independent Prozor Battalion was located at the time of this order.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And would you confirm that as events proved, later on the Prozor Independent Battalion did indeed fight in a battle in the area of Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was opposite its area of responsibility. The battalion was deployed to that area. This was the area of responsibility of the Prozor Independent Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the answer to my question is yes, is it not?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it only logical that the battalion was charged with -- with providing defence within its area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And according to the normal chain of command, you received this document on or about the 29th of August, as dated; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Well, I offer that document. Thank you. At around that time, on the 29th -- perhaps I'll preface my next question with this: Appreciating that you don't have a precise memory for exact dates, do you accept that on or about the 29th of August an inspection team arrived in your zone of operation consisting of Rifat Bilajac, Zicro Suljevic, Vehbija Karic, and one other individual whose name escapes me, but I think it might be Hubic, H-u-b-i-c.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall this man Hubic either. But a lot of time has elapsed and I cannot confirm with certainty, but it is true that shortly afterwards this team of people did come to the area of responsibility of the corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, could I -- Mr. Gusic, let me assure you I'm not going to pick a quarrel on the topic of Mr. Hubic, but he's mentioned on an order which I'm about to show you, so that's why I mention him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But could the witness please be shown Defence document --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: D15, and it's DD00.0053, and it will be -- it's to be marked MFI141.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I have it on full screen? That's better.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, do you see that there's an order from -- sorry, just using your knowledge of the way orders are constructed. You can see there that this is an order from the 29th of August, 1993 which authorises a team consisting of the four individuals I just mentioned to coordinate combat operations between the 4th and the 6th Corps in the Neretva River Valley and to perform another function regarding the 3rd and the 6th Corps.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By the terms of that order, you don't suggest that any of those individuals have got the power to issue commands to combat units in that area, do you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not an order. I just want to give you my comment. This is an authorisation whereby this team is authorised to coordinate, which means to provide a specialist assistant and coordinate actions. So that's what it's about. This is the first time I see this document, but I did not necessarily have to see it, because there were people in the field and if I ever had any doubts as to what had been asked of me, they could have shown it to me. I really don't recall him being down there. He might have. But I do recall the three generals -- or rather, one of them was a brigadier. So I remember the three of them being there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a quick matter of terminology. None of these people were brigadiers or generals at that time, were they?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not really. But if you don't mind --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, they were senior staff officers effectively.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And -- and each of them, because of their experience and -- and perhaps also their age -- well, I'll withdraw that. I'll ask you questions about the most senior person in the field doctrine a bit later on. Very well. Now, with regard to those people there, you can see that the preamble to this authorisation provides that it's done with the objective of coordinating combat operations. Now, I just want you to focus on that word "coordinating" for a moment. Coordinating -- the power to coordinate is very different to the power to command, isn't it? It's a different function altogether.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this authorisation, for them to be able to command, it would have to say that in accordance with their opinions they were able to reach decisions. But this is missing. So this means they were not able to command troops on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I appreciate you didn't see this -- you've got no recollection of seeing this document, but I take it -- well, I suggest to you that being senior and sensible staff officers, they would have made it -- they, being Karic, Suljevic, Bilajac -- would have made it quite clear to you what they were doing in the area, seeing as you were the corps commander in the area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. But I was not bound by their opinion. If I made a decision different from theirs, they would probably inform the commander right away. That is the role of coordination. But I was not bound by their requests. I did not have to make decisions in accordance with what they were offering me. But they could influence my decisions by reporting to the commander on any decisions I made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I offer that document for tender.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And perhaps for completeness on that question, they told you -- when you -- when you met these three at the end of August, they told you nothing to contradict what was in that order, did they? In other words -- sorry, perhaps I'll put that a different way. What they told you about their role was consistent with what's contained in that order; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think they mentioned the authorisation at all. As I said, they often came to my command even before this document was issued. They were assisting me, because I did not have the required experience, the experience required by the situation. So these were people I frequently consulted. I'm sure I never asked for this document or saw it, nor was there any need for them to mention it. I felt that their presence in my area of responsibility was a great contribution because I could only gain by their presence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Gusic, I think perhaps my question wasn't very clear there. I'm not suggesting that you should have demanded the document. What I'm putting to you is they told you they were there in the area with the objective of coordinating combat operations and that they were there to coordinate combat operations between the 4th and the 6th Corps in the Neretva Valley and between the 4th and the 6th Corps in the Vrbas River Valley and the general Fojnica area. Do you agree that that's in broad terms that's what they told you at that time?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were members of the superior command and they knew what my tasks were and they came to assist me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So I've got some questions -- so that brings us to the end of that week. And what's happened in that week is that you've been -- so you agree in summary that the week after Zenica, you were given some tasks by Delic, you were given a report by your intelligence chief, which we've tendered, and -- and Karic, Suljevic, Bilajac arrived to perform -- to perform --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Intelligence. Intelligence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, pardon me, yes. Thank you for that correction. But that's the case, isn't it? Those three things happened?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And he was not an assistant. He was neither a chief or an assistant. He was just an ordinary officer of the intelligence organ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to take you now - and perhaps the Court should be aware of what's about to come here - Mr. Gusic, to some matters of doctrine which lie behind the drafting of orders. And perhaps I -- I mention that it's important to do this in the abstract in order to explain certain matters that come later on. So that I'm going to take you to that now. Now, first of all, is there a system within the army known as RIK, that is, commander and control?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't get a --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My apologies. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, RIK. RIK. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I'll come to the details of that in a moment. But is there overlying the whole system of command and control a principle known as the principle of single authority?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to read you a passage, and you tell me if you agree with this as a relatively adequate summary of the principle of single authority or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a passage I'm going to read. It's about eight lines long or so, so -- so that's what's coming.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the quote is this: "In the system, RIK, consists of the inviolable right of the commander to command and control subordinated units, ensuring the appearance of only one superior in command and control who commands. It is the right of the commander to make decisions, so he alone bears the responsibility for this. The commander can transfer some of his rights and obligations to the Chief of Staff, assistants, or subordinated commanders but he cannot transfer responsibility for the state and use of units. The command relationship is established by the principle of subordination in a military organisation. A command relationship is founded on the duty, right, and responsibility of superiors to make decisions and designate tasks and the duty, right, and responsibility of subordinates to carry out these tasks."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Morrissey, would you please lay a foundation for that quotation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I indicate it's something that's likely to be led in evidence in the Defence case from a witness. It's not -- I'm not seeking to put it as an authoritative quote from a rule. Perhaps I shouldn't have used the term "quote" at all. It's not my words. It's just somebody who initially understood this better than I did. And I use the term "quote" because I'm quoting from the notes that I have. I'm not putting a document to him as an authoritative document. I'm putting it as a view which he may choose to adopt. I do not seek to put it as something that I rely on independently in any way. And, yes, I apologise, I did use the word "quote" at the start. Your Honour is right to point it out. But that's what I'm doing. I'm putting a view which I'm inviting him to adopt, to reject, or perhaps comment on it in various aspects. And I'll seek to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Ms. Chana.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I'm sorry if I interrupted counsel. I have no objection to this quote being shown as a rule, but it's such a long quote, and I think it's not fair to the witness to be able to try and remember and questions -- I think a quote of this length should be before the witness for him to see as he answers questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. In principle, I agree with you. But we will see how much the witness get it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can now advance the situation. This is taken from a Prosecution document, the original of which is called [B/C/S spoken] and with which the witness might be vague and ambiguous. And if it would assist, I'll just give it to the witness. The witness would know this book, I would think, better than anyone else in the court; at least that side of the court. So it has -- it has a 65 ter number -- a Prosecution number P117. And the -- and the relevant scan numbers are L0063322-L0063474. And what we're seeking is pages 27 to 28. The heading is -- in English, the heading is on page 27 and the bulk of the text is on page 28.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Gusic, has that appeared on the screen or is it being sought still?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. We'd seek that that be turned to page 27 and 28. In B/C/S, 25. So Mr. Gusic will need 25.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you just put the beginning of the page, because I don't have the chapter entitled "Single authority." I think we need the previous page. I think it must be on page 27. Because what I see here is "Operativeness and secrecy." I wish to comply with what I am being asked, but I'd like to see what it's about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course. One moment, please. Mr. Gusic, just one moment please. Can I inquire what page number you have in front of you there in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Could Mr. Gusic please be shown the B/C/S version 25. It's the English version that needs to be page 27. While that's being done, can I indicate to the Court as a sign of what must be seen as intellectual cowardice I had obviously copied in my notes the precise terms of the manual which I was proposing to put at the end of this line of questioning. So I apologise for reading it out if was my own. I don't know where I got that idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you now have page 25 in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the middle of that page, is there a section headed "Single authority"?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, "Single authority." That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, rather than reading it out again and torturing the Court and the witness, do you agree that that passage there accurately states in a brief and manageable form the meaning of the concept of single authority?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This here is the principle. It discusses the principle of single authority. However, there is a more detailed account, more precise, and that's in the rules of service. There is a chapter there on subordination and superiority. This is simply the principle governing the rules.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, should there be a need to go to that detail, that will be done. But we have to proceed at a certain level of generality in this court, and you confirm that that is -- that that's an accurate statement of the general overarching principle of single authority?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But it is clarified in greater detail in the rules of service more precisely, and the rules of service were binding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I tender -- I offer that for tender -- in fact, I'd seek to tender those rules now at this stage. They would be MFI412 -- sorry, 142. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, there's one more matter that I would seek to -- to ask you to explain, and that is the five functions of command and control. Do you agree that under the heading of command and control there are five distinct functions, the names of which I'll now read to you: One, planning; two, organisation; three, command; four, coordination; and five, control?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it accurate at this high level of generality of principle to state that the system of command and control, RIK, contains "command" as one of five elements?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of this is command and control. I can't say there's only one element called "command." All of this is command. The five elements you listed contains "command," which is understood to mean issuing orders directly. But all these five elements together constitute command and control. We would be going very far if we were now to analyse what "command" means and what "control" means. It would take a long time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, don't be concerned by that question of time for this purpose. The word "rukovodjenje" is a distinct word from the word "komandovanje," isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly, yes. Control, to try explain it, is something similar to direction or management; while "command" implies these five elements, because simply issuing an order without planning and without taking into account all these five points, is not a proper order. An order has to have its five basic points. All of this together is command. And in the context of your question, the command element that you listed implies issuing orders, but all of this together is command and control. "Control," however, does not imply issuing orders. Services and control and commands command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And in short, the term "rukovodjenje" - and you'll have to forgive me for the pronunciation problems.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Rukovedjenje" itself, that word alone, does not include the power to command but refers to the other, one might say, more --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Whereas command --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These five functions refer both to command and control. I cannot assert that "command" means simply issuing orders. No, "command" is not merely issuing orders. There has to be an assessment, a plan, a decision, a task, a coordination, who is to do what, and there has to be control, how this is to be executed. All of this is command. So mere issuing of orders is not commanding. Anyone can read an order, but the entire system of command is more complex than what you are trying to say. What you're talking about is simply issuing orders; whereas, "command" includes -- "command and control" includes all the five elements you listed. I agree with that. When you are talking about control, "rukovodjenje," unlike "command," it means you can control personnel, certain services, give guidelines. It's more like management. It's more management than command. In the case of command, you're assigning tasks. That's why I cannot agree that any one of the five elements you listed can be excluded. All of them together constitute command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Very well. We now leave the area -- the realm of general principle for a moment in relation to military doctrine and turn to some questions governing the powers of the Chief of Staff, the powers of the deputy, and also some questions about what is the effect of the most senior person on the terrain. And just so that you understand, we remain in chronological terms. We remain at the end of -- at the end of August effectively, having analysed Zenica, having gone through that last week when the 6th Corps was undertaking the actions that you've indicated. We're now pausing for these management sort of issues in order to lay a basis for future questions. Now, I have some questions for you about the Chief of Staff and his or, indeed in theory, her functions. You were questioned by the Prosecutor on Thursday about the powers attaching to the Chief of Staff, the powers attaching to deputy commanders, and the powers attaching to most senior people in the field. Do you recall that series of questions?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And isn't the -- the fact that -- I just want to do a very brief background question here. I promise not to get sidetracked in it too much. The Bosnian army effectively evolved out of the TO, the territorial organisation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You'll have to speak because it's recording. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And without going into the -- the precise appointments --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not just the Territorial Defence. One unit was Territorial Defence, but there were other units. There was the MUP, the reserve MUP forces, the units of the Patriotic League, the units of the Green Berets. There were different kinds of units. But the largest force were the reserve MUP forces and the TO forces -- or rather, the Armed Forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you referred to the Green Berets, you're referring to one of the many, if you like, local units that sprang up as volunteers under a leader that -- that the unit effectively chose for itself; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've lost any audio connection.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that I personally selected them. These were volunteers. I didn't choose them. This was a movement. I see it as a movement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And although the -- look, I won't ask you for general comments. I'll just -- we'll do that if we get the chance a bit later on. Anyway, certainly by later in -- in -- in 1992, Sefer Halilovic was effectively the senior military commander; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was my commander, among other things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the head of the armed forces per se was in fact Alija Izetbegovic, the president?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the civilian commander, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, as we've seen -- now, you are a person who's very -- you don't wish to be -- or you didn't wish at the time to be involved in the politics of Bosnia but you wished simply to serve as a soldier. Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I attempted to adhere to that up to the end of my career, to remain simply a soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Mr. Gusic, without attempting to draw you personally in any way into a political dispute, you remember Sefer Halilovic's political position as he articulated it at Zenica was against the partition of Bosnia under the plans such as the Vance-Owen Plan or the Stoltenberg Plan; do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, we've had evidence already that on the 8th of June of 1993 Sefer Halilovic ceased to be the commanding officer in the army and was replaced effectively in that condition by Rasim Delic, who took up a newly created position as commander; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Sefer Halilovic was in charge of the army, people used to -- in the absence of formal ranks, people often used to refer to him as simply "chief"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Chief, commander, depending on the situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the ground, the soldiers addressed him as "commander." But his close collaborators probably addressed him as "chief."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, once Commander Delic became the commander on the 8th, Sefer Halilovic functioned as the Chief of Staff of the Bosnian armed forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was both deputy commander and Chief of Staff, because the OTP showed the order where both these functions are listed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll stop you there --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I didn't see it up until the moment --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. I just want to stop you for one moment. This is an important matter or can be an important matter later. He became the deputy -- now, what I want to put to you is that he became the deputy commander only five weeks later, when he was appointed under -- under another order to be both Chief of Staff and deputy, that order being dated the 18th of July of 1993.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the date of the order I was looking at, but if I saw it clearly - and I told you that I didn't have to see the order and that I only saw it here - it seems to me that this is the order that the OTP showed to me where it says that he was also deputy commander. I don't want to sound as if I'm contradicting myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no, no, Mr. Gusic. There's no -- it's okay. I'm going to show you the order so that you can comment on it, and don't be concerned about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Could the witness please be shown D110. And I'll just provide you with the relevant numbers. It's DD00.0439, and it's to be marked for exhibit 143, 143.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, what I'm going to do is show you this order, and I'm going to ask you to look at a couple of details of it in terms of the power that was given to Sefer Halilovic. While that document is being brought up, I'll just ask you some general questions, if I may.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the first page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. Okay. Well, just -- you can look at it if you feel that you need to, but just let me ask you some other questions first before I take you directly to it. Normally speaking, a Chief of Staff has certain functions. It has certain branches of the staff attached to his office. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as far as you know, the usual situation is that the Chief of Staff has got authority over the intelligence administration section; is that correct? In the normal course of events, that's what a Chief of Staff has?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And also has --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Over the administration for intelligence affairs, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And also, the Chief of Staff normally has direct control over the -- over the organ for mobilisation and organisation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, it's an administration. You're talking about the Chief of Staff at the level of the Army of BiH.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, what I want to do now is to get you to look, please -- the page that's currently on is page 1. Could we please have the following page, page 2. We're just going to get you another page, Mr. Gusic. In fact, the -- it's likely to be page 3, but if we take page 2 first and see if that's the one. Okay. Page 2 is the correct page. Now, this decision has got two matters of importance. Because we're talking about Chief of Staff, I'd like you to look at Roman numeral III and look at number 3 underneath that.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you see here it describes the office of the Chief of Staff -- of the Chief of the Main Staff command operations centre.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he's -- it says that: "The Chief of the Main Staff is directly linked" -- sorry. Pardon me. I'll take that -- I take a step back from that. This section directly links the office of the chief, the command operations centre, the headquarters, administration, and combat arms administration section. It directly links those to the Chief of the Main Staff. Do you agree with that? It's in the first sentence there, and I may be phrasing it wrongly, but ...

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's item 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's all the organs and units linked to the Chief of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Correct. But would you please look now at the second sentence. And I'll read it with you. It says: "The RV" - that's the air force - "PVO," anti-aircraft defence, administration, "intelligence administration, organisation and mobilisation administration, and training, education, rules and regulations administration and the navy are indirectly linked to the Chief of the Main Staff and directly to the Main Staff commander." Now, looking at that document, what that shows you, does it -- isn't it, is that Sefer Halilovic as Chief of Staff was in fact deprived of the usual control that a Chief of Staff has with respect to the specifics, intelligence administration and organisation and mobilisation administration? Do you agree with that proposition, looking at that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partly, yes. Because here there's the direct link with the commander, yes. But that doesn't mean that he had no links with these administrations. This was partly conditioned by the direct link that the commander had. Now, what this actually meant, the persons who would be best placed to answer that would be the Chief of the Main Staff and the commander himself. But the way I can interpret it is that the commander has the direct link and the Chief of Staff has the indirect link, and that's not item number 2, as you said a minute ago, but item number 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I thought I'd said 3, but in any event you're correct that 3 is the one I'm referring to. Mr. Gusic, can I put another interpretation to you and you tell me if you agree with this. What this represents is an attempt by the leadership of Bosnia to make sure that Sefer Halilovic was given as little power as possible as Chief of Staff. Do you agree with that or not?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, you're inviting me to make a comment on something that I am not aware of and cannot comment upon. It is a bit peculiar, the provision as I see it here, and I don't know what reasons lay behind this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let me just -- I'll have to -- because we've got the document open in front of us now, I have to jump forward to a section that concerns deputies. I'm sorry it is out of order, but because the document is here, it will save time. Would you please just look to paragraph 1 that's on the page in front of you there, still under Roman numeral III, and look at the second paragraph of that. Does that provide now that: "The Main Staff consists of Main Staff commander, Main Staff commander's office, three deputy commanders (Muslim, Serb, and Croat), the commander operations centre with headquarters administration, branches, combat armed forces, and support arms administration. The Chief of the Main Staff is also deputy commander according to the establishment." Now, do you agree that by virtue of that last sentence there Sefer Halilovic became ex officio as Chief of Staff also a deputy commander and that's how he came to be a deputy commander?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, you're inviting me to provide a comment that I cannot give you with certainty. I cannot say how it was that it came about that he became deputy commander. But it is a fact that he was deputy commander. And now you're suggesting that this was ex officio. Now, I really don't know whether he became deputy on the basis of that or whether it was on the basis of -- of his knowledge and the influence that he exerted on the arms developments in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it's quite obvious -- I understand you don't want to speculate, but you don't have to. If you look at that last sentence, it's quite clear that the Chief of Staff becomes the deputy commander simply by being the Chief of Staff. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how to comment on this. I am not an author of this order, nor did I have occasion to look at this order earlier on and examine it more closely. I don't believe that his function as Chief of Staff was the reason why he became deputy. I believe that Sefer Halilovic was one of the men who was rightly placed and that he was one of the deserving officers in the initial stages of defence. Now, if you're asking me to agree with what you're saying, I cannot agree with that. Now, I can only go into the realm of interpreting, and I've already told you that I do not wish to interpret the orders of my superiors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. All right. Thank you, Mr. Gusic. Well, now I want to ask you some questions about the powers of the Chief of Staff. We'll come back the that deputies issue, and I really raised it because I occur there is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: May I offer that document for tender, please. Could I turn now to the question of the powers of Chief of Staff to issue commands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the past, you have been asked questions about the powers of Chiefs of Staff by -- by investigators from the -- from the Office of the Prosecutor here and -- sorry, you'll just have to excuse me a moment here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say on the 16th of November 2000 in a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor at page 5 as follows? I'm quoting now from that statement: "As far as I remember, there were no written regulations in the BH army, in the Bosnian army, concerning the Chief of Staff. In practice, in the Bosnian army the Chief of Staff did not have the power to" -- sorry, "did not have the authority to issue binding orders. Only in one case could this Chief of Staff issue binding orders, and this was if the corps commander gave him such authority in writing. His only authority was that he could order commanders of units to provide him with information about the unit and order reports from them. The Chief of Staff could not give binding orders to military security, military intelligence, or military police." And in the context of which you spoke, you went on to say: "This was the prerogative of the corps commander." Now, do you acknowledge the truth of what you said to the -- to the investigator at that time?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said is what is contained in the rules that you showed to me now during your examination. I was merely saying what was contained in the regulations. I never saw this particular decree, and that's why I spoke from memory that I believed that there were no other regulations concerning Chiefs of Staffs, but I was not aware of the provision -- any special instruction for the Chief of Staff -- of the Main Staff other than those that were assumed from the JNA. I don't think that there were any Bosnian ones, and I -- in the period of time we are talking about, for the lower levels, and I still believe so today. Whereas, at the time I didn't necessarily have to know whether there were such instructions because I wasn't at that level of command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's one other thing that you said. And I'd just ask you to adopt the truth of this. This is at page 3 of the statement dated 16 to 17 November 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And could it I point out to the Tribunal that he was interviewed on the same dates in 2000 and in 2001, so you have to look at the -- at the years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said: "In disciplinary terms, the Chief of Command Staff could not directly punish any corps or brigade commander for any failures, omissions, or violation of military discipline or law. However, he could suggest to the commander of the Supreme Command Staff to take disciplinary measures against the corps commander or any other commanders." Is that true and is it based on the rules as you've described?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Unless he had the authority to command and then there was breach of discipline in the course of a task being executed, he could in that case impose some sort of a measure that he was authorised for, but under normal circumstances this fell exclusively under the competence of the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excellent. Could I turn now to the deputy commander issue. Now, as deputy -- a deputy commander could exercise command powers if and only if authorised to do so by the commanding officer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about the level that I'm familiar with, but I suppose that the same is true for the Main Staff. It is true that he had to have the authority of the commander to issue commands. And if we're talking about normal circumstances, then usually the deputy would have some duties related to the TO staffs on the strength of the corps. I'm talking about this territorial principle of commanding. Whereas, the manoeuvre type of commanding was entirely within the authority of the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, to summarise therefore the position relating to Chiefs of Staff and deputies, you can't infer that a Chief of Staff is in command of a particular operation merely because he is the Chief of Staff. In order to find that he's the commander of an operation, you need to point to an order authorising him to command that operation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that's quite customary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the same applies for deputy commanders. A deputy commander can command an operation but there needs to be an order specifically permitting him to do so before he can; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's one and the same thing. But I don't want to contradict what I said on Thursday, because at the time -- the period of time we were referring to, there were no ranks, so people used to sign their orders with their function. So they would put "deputy commander" in addition to his name. So you'd always have the function discharging by the person and then the name of the person signing. So the function was something that was placed at the time instead of a rank. However, of course, this person was unable to issue any such orders without having been authorised by the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was an additional reason why -- and sorry, and perhaps I should say this: The custom was and in fact the rule was for deputy commanders when signing an order as deputy to sign it, for example, "Stjepan Siber" on behalf of the commander Rasim Delic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now you're actually cornering me to say that for a given period of time the practice was different than the one I just mentioned. There was the custom of signing with a "for," meaning "on behalf." You would have a person signing "for" and then signing in their hand. So if we received this letter by electronic mail, we would not know whether it was signed by Rasim Delic or one of his deputies. Later on they would write "under the authorisation of the commander," and then the function and the name. Now, I can't really remember whether it also applied to this period in time that you would write "under the authorisation of" a given person and then you would write your full name and function. So there were different practices at different points in time. But one should be able to trace and find these orders in the files, to find out -- to establish what the practice was in a given period of time. But you are right; there was a period in time when you were obligated to write "under the authorisation" of a given officer and then your name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I just indicate -- I understand we've gone a couple of minutes past the time designated, but this section can be finished in about 60 seconds and I'd just seek the Court's indulgence, if you don't mind. And I'm grateful for it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to conclude that matter. If the orders before this Court shows Stjepan Siber signing in the way that I suggested on the 4th of September and on the 16th of September, you wouldn't dispute that that was the practice at that time, would you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. The final question is that -- in terms of deputies, there was a -- an additional reason why clarity was needed in giving authority to deputies. When Rasim Delic had to authorise a deputy, unlike most commanders, he had to make a choice between three deputies, didn't he, pursuant to that order I just showed you of the 18th?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is definitely the case. This lay within his authority to take decisions, and there was probably some sort of an order, a procedure in place that he had to follow that I am not aware of, but it was either his own discretion or there was a procedure in place for him to follow, some sort of a schedule so to say, maybe on a rotational basis, when was such-and-such's turn to be given authorisation. So there are three possible options of how this could have taken place, but I don't -- I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You've been shown -- or there's been evidence in this court and there'll be more evidence frankly of orders by Stjepan Siber signed on behalf of Commander Delic. What I'm going to ask you now is: Can you point to any order signed by Sefer Halilovic as deputy on behalf of Commander Delic within your own knowledge?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That he was deputy, that he signed both as deputy and Chief of Staff you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. I just want you to point to any order where he signed as deputy. Whether as Chief of Staff as well or not, I don't mind. But a single order. Just -- you tell us if you know of one or if you've seen one and if you have one, where he signed as deputy.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was talking to the Prosecutor, I saw an order where it said "Chief of Staff," and below that "deputy commander." So I did see one such document during proofing. But I can't tell you what the contents of the order are. I did see it though. There were both functions signed there. I never saw, however, only the function of deputy commander being signed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that map that's behind you, is there any mention of deputy?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm going to move to a new topic, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll take a break for 20 minutes. We'll resume at quarter to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Your microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, and sorry to the interpreters. Could I indicate for the convenience of the Court I will not finish by the appropriate time today. I expect to finish very comfortably within tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. But we have to stop today at 1.45 because I don't want to eat time of the next case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. As the Court pleases. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I've completed my questions now about the Chief of Staff and about the deputy. The Prosecution also asked you questions about the powers to command attaching to the most senior officer present. I want to just ask you about an example. You will recall I showed you a minute ago an order dated the 26th of August from Commander Delic to you ordering -- ordering you to participate in certain combat activities in the Neretva Valley. Do you recall me showing you that particular document?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, clearly you were bound to obey that direct order of your commander; correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was carried out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, if Zicro Suljevic arrived at your corps headquarters the day after you received that order and told you, "Do not carry out the order of Rasim Delic," was that order of Suljevic binding on you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is the fact that --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But if General Suljevic had made that comment, I would have told General Delic about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I'm going to get to that in a moment. And I understand your answer. But of course if Suljevic had authorisation from Delic to do that, then his order does become binding; correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But he only had an order to coordinate combat operations, not to annul the orders issued by the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I'm using this as an example to test a particular proposition -- not a proposition I understand you to be advancing but a proposition nevertheless. And that is this: That Suljevic was, if you like, a senior commander to you, in terms of experience, age, and rank in the former JNA and all the other indicators. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, not in the position he held down there. The authorisation he had was only to coordinate combat operations, not to change any decisions regarding the combat operations. It said explicitly in his authorisation and that General Suljevic never attempted to overstep that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I -- Mr. Gusic, do you understand that I was -- I was putting a hypothetical to you in that situation?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he could have -- had he been authorised, he could have been superior to me, but he never showed me any such authorisation nor did he ever invoke it. But in principle yes, the commander could have authorised him to do that. He could have written an order authorising him to do that, but I know he never had any such authorisation, nor did he show it to me, nor did he take any such measures. He never attempted to issue orders to me. He never ordered me to do anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at a general level, is it the fact that the question of whether a senior -- a more senior officer can command perhaps someone of less experience really depends not so much on their seniority but on the nature of the authority given to them by the commander? Is that a fair proposition?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander or whoever was with the commander. It worked two ways. But yes, authorisation was very important.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now, I want to turn now to the -- to the order given by Commander Delic to the inspection team in which he appointed Sefer Halilovic as head of that team.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And could the witness please be shown MFI108.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, you've looked at this already.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Actually, I just wish to recant that one. I'm terribly sorry. Could the witness first be shown another order. I apologise for that. And that is my fault. My notes were not in order. Could the witness please be shown Defence document D41, the number of which is DD00.0123. And it's to be marked for exhibit as MFI144.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, I apologise for that sudden change. There's a document I want to show you first before we get to the Delic order.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, does this appear to be an order from back in the year -- the year 1992 dated the 20th of August appointing -- just excuse me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just excuse me, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry. Before I ask you that question, could the witness please be shown the following page.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen that page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, is the document you're looking at there a document which appoints an individual to command -- to a temporary command, that individual being Dzemal Najetovic?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in addition, do you see the second in command there is Asim Dzambasovic, who's also present in court here, being appointed as Chief of Staff and deputy commander of that temporary command?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, does this order plainly and unequivocally state who is the commander?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does it --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not an order. This is an appointment. And since you're asking, probably because of the time in which it was written, you can't see what formation this is. This is a command group. But of what? It doesn't say. You can see clearly, however, who the commander is and the officers assigned certain sections.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's -- could we just go back now to the -- to the first page. Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have it now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, do you have here a decision creating a temporary command, JUG.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is the effect of this decision an appointment which you have before you to clearly state what the temporary command is and who is to be in command of it?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't say clearly what this temporary command is, but it does state clearly who is at its head. In item 2, the appointed commander is authorised to form an organisational structure, so the commander will say what it is. He is authorised to say what is being formed. But that's not specified in this document. It forms only a command, not a unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, because it forms only a command and not a unit, that decision explicitly gives the power to that command to organise the unit subsequently; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Gusic, you have to speak because it's recording --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To form a unit or a temporary formation, such as an operational group or a combat group or something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I offer that for tender.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Gusic, the reason I showed you that document is to -- to enable you to comment on a proposition I want to put, that is, that in the Bosnian army in -- in its early two years because of the situation, because people -- because many of the officers and soldiers were not trained, because there were some commanders who from time to time didn't like to obey every order they were given, and for all the reasons that we've heard about in this court, it was very important that when a person was appointed to a command, that the person being appointed to the command be clearly explained in an order. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992, yes. Later on, there was a procedure to be followed and it was slightly different, in the period after that. In 1992, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in general -- well, perhaps I want to put this to you: In 1993, it was still crucially important that the creation of command responsibility for any individual be made perfectly clear so that there could be no confusion and no breach of the single line of authority which is so important in military matters. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When a certain organisation was established, it was known who was at the head of the army, who the corps commanders were, who the brigade commanders were, so this whole procedure had already been defined. Authorisation within the framework of posts to which people were appointed followed from specific tasks. Depending on the task at hand, appointments were written or authorisation to command was given.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. Now, with apologies again to the court staff, may I return, please, to the document, marked for exhibit 108, that being the order of the 30th of August from Commander Delic. Okay. Do you have the document, Mr. Gusic?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, could I just put some general propositions to you about this order first of all. Firstly, you agree with this --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, sorry, something has just occurred to confuse us. That's okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, sorry, it's not your problem. Would you please now, just looking at that document, confirm this: There is no reference to any particular military operation -- well, perhaps I'll put it another way. There's no -- there's no reference to Operation Neretva 93 at all on that document, is there?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it follows blindingly obviously that there is no commander of Operation Neretva 93 mentioned on that document. Is that also correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, what you say is that at this time, that being the 30th of August, 1993, you'd never even heard the name Neretva 1993 -- or Neretva 93, I'm sorry; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's correct, that is. I hadn't heard of the name of the operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So whatever the basis is upon which Sefer Halilovic acted later on, this order does not appoint Sefer Halilovic to be the commander of Operation Neretva 93; do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is not appointed by this order, but it gives him the possibility of planning and conducting the operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In item 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I'm going to come to each item in -- in due course, Mr. Gusic. But at all events, you agree with my primary proposition, don't you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, look at the preamble at paragraph 1 and the bit -- the preamble that comes before the words "I order." That -- the preamble of that focuses upon conclusions reached at the consultations between members of the supreme HQ and corps commanders by which I take it -- you would take it to be a reference to the Zenica conclusions? Or perhaps I won't ask you to speculate, but does that appear to be consistent -- does that appear to you to be consistent with the Zenica conclusions as you knew them to be?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because there was no other meeting apart from that one in this period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And it -- and it specifically aims -- addresses the aim of eliminating current shortcomings and weaknesses in the zones of responsibility of the 4th and 6th Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not going to bring it up on the screen now unless you positively need it to be done, but you'll recall I showed you a document earlier which was the document with the four people in the inspection team, Karic, Suljevic, Bilajac, and Hubic? Do you recall that document?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall that that referred to coordinating combat activities?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that -- well, I'll come back to that, but anyway, you recall it. Now, look at -- under the order. The main tasks of the team are as follows. And do you see that it sets out four main tasks for the team?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I want to ask you a question about the first of those four tasks. Could you just look at that closely.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you remember that you explained before the break to this Court the meaning of the word "rukovodjenje." Do you remember explaining the meaning of that word?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you -- you used terms -- you can't comment on the translation, of course, but you used -- but as words to help explain the meaning of that term to the lay people here, you equated "rukovodjenje" to some degree with the concept of management or the concept of direction. Is that an accurate way of paraphrasing what you told us about that word?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes. It is, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you just tell us that -- at the end of that sentence, could -- well, would you please read the sentence out to the Court in your language, in Bosnian, that first one.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the first subparagraph in paragraph 1?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's exactly what I mean, yes. Read it to the end.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Review of the combat readiness of the commands and units in the field and control of combat operations."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stop there. Thank you. It's that last phrase which was mentioned, "the control of combat operations." The word that you -- that has been translated to us as "control" is "rukovodjenje"; correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where does the word "rukovodjenje" appear in the -- in the Bosnian version that you have in front of you there?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Rukovodjenje" can mean "management," but "kontrola" [phoen] may not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But the word that's used in the original document in the original order is "rukovodjenje" and not "komondovanje"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've already explained the difference between those two words, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Several times.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But now you say -- you now say that "rukovodjenje" equals "kontrola." This is not correct because kontrola is only one element of command and control or "komondovanje rukovodjenje."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But although you -- you are correct to -- well, perhaps -- I say -- you say that I should not substitute "kontrola" for "rukovodjenje" but you'd equally agree that no one should substitute "komondovanje" for "rukovodjenje" in that context.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, please. "Rukovodjenje" has five principles, just like "komondovanje." It has five principles. "Kontrola" is one of the elements of issuing specific orders In order to be sure that an order has been carried out, we need to control or monitor this. This is only a small segment of command. "Kontrola" in "rukovodjenje" is only a segment of what we are conveying to the people we are managing, whether they are carrying this out or not, whether they are complying. "Rukovodjenje" cannot be the same as "kontrola." It includes "kontrola." It includes an element of control but it cannot be control only. It is a much broader concept.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, I -- I must have misled you about the nature of the questions, because you have made that clear already and -- and I'm not attacking you about it. You -- I think you did answer my question, and I'm sorry if I suggested that I was attempting -- I'm sorry if I tried to suggest that "kontrola" equals "rukovodjenje," because that's not our position, and I understand very well it's not your position. Could I ask you to look at the second of those prongs, and perhaps also just glance at the third and the forth of those as well.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it's true to say that those four tasks are classic staff functions, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, both the staff and the command. They are classic command functions, not only functions of the staff but also of the command, because this part which refers to cooperating with civilian authorities, this is a function falling outside the domain of the staff. These are functions of the command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You'll just have to excuse me. Sorry, Mr. Gusic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, just -- there may be an interpretation problem here of some significance, so I would ask you, please, to read out paragraph 1 -- just a moment -- just a minute -- commencing at -- you see the words "I hereby order"?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see that, but I do see the entire paragraph 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, could you please read -- and read slowly so that we can have it interpreted to us, because there may be something missing from the English version that seems to have been provided here. Would you please just read from -- from that -- the words "I hereby order" or "I order," and the interpreters will -- will interpret and we'll then know what it says.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Form a professional inspection team to coordinate the work and tasks in the zone of responsibility of the 4th and 6th Corps. The main tasks of the team are as follows: Review of the combat readiness of the commands and units in the field and rukovodjenje of combat operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Just stop there for a moment, please, Mr. Gusic. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's evident that the English translation is missing. And I don't know if it's missing on yours. I presume we're looking at the same thing. It's quite evident that there is a -- a segment missing, and the segment says "Form a professional inspection team to coordinate the work and tasks in the zone of responsibility of the 4th and 6th Corps."

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Chana.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I might be able to assist in this. I asked our case manager to look up, and we have -- there were two translations done on this particular document, and this is not the one which had been put forward. The one we have is this particular passage that counsel is trying to read, it says "To evaluate the combat readiness of the command units in the field to direct combat operations," is what the CLSS translation -- the word is -- we can put it on the ELMO, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it seems to me that there are several places missing in the English text in front of me at least.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: This is a document used, I believe, by both parties in the direct and cross-examination. And could I order that the language section of this Tribunal check the language in this document compared with the two versions of the translations this afternoon and, if possible, to provide us with a more or less correct copy for tomorrow because tomorrow I'm sure that we are going to deal with the admission issues. I want to admit the most correct document, you know, into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I assist the Court in this regard. The Defence has prepared a -- or has had prepared a further revised translation of this document. Now -- perhaps -- might I just say -- sorry, could I just issue an apology to Mr. Gusic. This has got nothing to do with him. It's a translation issue and perhaps he should be made aware of that. That, Your Honour, what we have is -- we've got copies of this. And perhaps if I could -- if I could provide hard copies for the purpose of discussion now because it's a matter of some significance. So could I provide these.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So you are suggesting that at this moment we will have three copies of the translation --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It may be -- it may be that this one will suffice as an accurate translation. I must say, Your Honour, I'm going to confess to be caught by something there. My learned assistant, legal assistant here, helped. But, Your Honour, we -- this translation is from the head of the CLSS translation division and it was done on a specific request for -- by us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Chana.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: This is a document the Prosecution has always been working on. This is the version that the CLSS translated and that's the one I used in my opening speech and that's the version I've been -- the Prosecution has put in as an exhibit. Now, Your Honour, obviously there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So at this proceedings, my suggestion is that we'll use the document, whatever available at this stage, and after today's sitting the language section will provide us with a more correct translation, taking into the consideration of the three copies of the translations. Am I right? Is it agreeable?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'm going to -- it will be agreeable unless Your Honour agrees to the other suggestion that I have, because it is -- it's a sensible one, if I may say so, with respect.
