But what's happened here, I should explain why it is that it's come up, because it's a matter of some significance, if you -- in this case, this is a command responsibility case, as the Court knows, and in one of the translations, at point 1, if you have on the -- the order in front of you there, you'll see the English order that's currently on the screen ends the sentence: "To estimate the combat readiness of the commands and units in the field and to command the combat operation." Now, the Defence says that that word "command" there is an absolute terrible error and that it's obviously wrong because the word used is "rukovodjenje" and not "komondovanje." I wonder if the Court now -- as a result of seeing that, we became aware of that sometime ago and we had intentions, which obviously events have passed by, of attempting a coup in cross-examination, which we now are not going able to do because events have moved past us. However, we did as a result of that have a -- what we think is a correct interpretation made, and that's the document that's been given to the court usher. Now, that's been done by the head of CLSS, and what might be acceptable is if we produce that now, have the inquiry made of CLSS that they authenticate it, but it's authenticated in the materials that's given, and proceed on that more correct document, if that's agreeable to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is this agreeable to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just take a moment to see what Mr. Morrissey has said?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I was not concentrating.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: While my friend is doing that, I might mention something else that -- it appears --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Wait a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I mean, I think that's -- that's probably the most sensible thing to do, is to eventually get the, as Mr. Morrissey said, CLSS to authenticate as to which one is the correct translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I mean, at this stage do you allow the Defence team to distribute the copy they believe is more authentic translation?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes. The -- the Defence counsel can continue with this line of cross-examination, but they must be -- have in mind, Your Honour that, we have a different translation and we just bring it to the attention of the Court. I don't know how much value that would be to continue in that regard, but we leave it to the Court whether it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is it possible to distribute forwards your copy at the same time?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I think that's probably -- would be more sensible, Your Honours, if they can have both as their -- as they examine this witness on the meaning and put it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Let's have the both copies distributed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are bound by what Your Honour says, and we'll proceed on that basis. But I just want to mention something else that's a matter of significance, that we think the Prosecution has two copies, two different and competing translations circulating in this court, because we saw one the other day where that word "command" on the second line was rendered as "direct." So that -- and I believe -- it was either shown on the Sanction system or during the opening, but I think it was done in evidence in chief with this witness on the Sanction system. And what that means is that there has been shown in this court a document that's new, that's different to what we had, and it would have to be said, quite frankly, different to what the Confirming Judge had, different to what the expert witness was shown, and in short different in a way that is -- well, the Court can see exactly how it's different and the evidence is quite plain as to how it's different, so I won't rehearse that. Now, we're concerned about that because the basis on which this whole case proceeds has been opened in rather broad terms, and the Court has extended some latitude in order to let the Prosecution develop its case. We have made our protest. Your Honours have made a ruling. But precision in terms is important. And if that document, as has always been part of the Prosecution's case, is said to form somehow part of the Neretva 93 command structure, which attaches to Halilovic, then it's a document which was always of central significance. And in that situation, to have two competing translations floating in the court, even before the Defence made its contribution by adding a third, is a matter of concern because it's just not clear that the Prosecution themselves know which version they want to run with, because they've shown two. Now, this is not an attempt to attribute impropriety or sneakiness at all. It's just a demonstration that -- that the Confirming Judge seems to have proceeded on the basis that this was an authority to command. And that's been shown and it's been shown to you now as command. Whereas, earlier in the case there was one that said "direct" and the evidence of the witness is pretty plain as to what it all means. So I make those comments. We'll have to make submissions about them tomorrow. The witness is now here. And if I might proceed with the questions, I will. But I think I have to put those matters on the map, otherwise it's going to become difficult to ...

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry may I just make one point so that my friend can respond now in general. It's for that reason, among others, that we ask for a detailed chain of custody of exhibits over a long period of time. We just wanted to know how this came about and how such a mistranslation could happen. And you'll see the comments made when the inquiry is made of CLSS. We've got correspondence from CLSS about it and frankly it's a weird error, a very big error. Well, it's one that could be detected even by me, frankly. That means it must be very big. So that -- yes, those are the matters that I'd raise now. We'd seek to make some submissions about them tomorrow while my friend can respond, and then I'll proceed with questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Chana.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just want to make this point which I'm advised by my case manager, that we did produce -- this is the translation of CLSS. We produced it. Only the technicians did not get it into the system. Otherwise, we would not have this problem we're having today had the technicians succeeded in getting it into the system after we displayed it on Sanction --

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: We showed it on ELMO and -- via the ELMO, and that's when it didn't get into the system. But be that as it may, Your Honours, I think that perhaps a short break now so we can go to CLSS and find out which is the definitive copy, because this is the Defence's own -- they have asked the CLSS to translate their copy, and that's why we have competing translations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think my friend misunderstood the point. The point is which of the two Prosecution ones do they want to rely on. We know that our one is different and we know that that will be discussed. The Prosecution have two of them. Now, let them say now clearly that this should not be something they need to go to CLSS about. It's something they can answer themselves, which of their two do they rely on? The one on the screen or the one that was shown earlier. So I'm sorry, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: We need an answer to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, another subject: Mr. Morrissey, could you please at this stage indicate how much time you still need to finish your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm just troubled by how long this section is going to take now, but leaving this section out of -- out of account as a wild card, I should think two hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Two hours?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I've covered most of the theoretical topics. There's now factual matters which -- which do involve documents, and that takes time. The theoretical topics are now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: My concern is that we have to finish the testimony of this witness tomorrow because on Wednesday and Thursday we'll have the videolink, you know, witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Otherwise, this witness has to stay here for another two or three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I -- I bear in mind those problems, and we -- Your Honour may have seen there's been some slicing of -- of -- of areas, but it's -- there are some areas that are just central to our case that I can't leave. And certainly in relation to the issues of deputies and Chiefs of Staff and so on, they were opened very broadly. And I have to shoot those down if I -- I have to deal with those. I mean, I have to endeavour to shoot those down. And -- and I have to do that in the abstract because the Prosecution led the evidence the way they did. I have completed so much of the cross-examination as I'm meaning to do on the theoretical side of it. This witness is now going to be cross-examined about this document, and as I indicated, about the -- the early days of the inspection team in Herzegovina, about the visit of Delic, the Dobro Polje meeting where plans were made, and we're going to part company. And then what happened after that, in terms of Grabovica, Uzdol, the involvement, if any, of this witness in that era, the cease-fire orders, and I've already finished after the 20th, as Your Honours will recall. We did that part quite early on. So that's what remains. It's directly relevant. None of it's scene-setting any more. It's all relevant material. I expect that we will finish this witness tomorrow, including redirect, including Your Honours' questions, even if they be relatively substantial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I hope you could have it done in 90 minutes, that is, one hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I shall set myself the goal. I -- yes, well, all I can say is I shall do my best, but it is -- this witness has given crucial evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I agree with you. And since this issue is a very important issue in this document which may be just a mere issue of translation, and at this moment we have three copies of the translation floating on the floor of this court, so we might stop here, which is about 12 minutes early, for today and ask the translation booths to give us a more proper or more correct translation by tomorrow. As for the reason why there's so many copies of the translation, I believe that we'll find some other time to look at it without the presence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll be guided by the Court, but I can certainly -- if it would assist, I can use the 12 minutes to ask questions about something else, if -- but it's a matter for Your Honour. If that seems to be an inelegant way, I'll stop now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if you change your topic, you're welcome to make the best use of the time available.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Well, Mr. Gusic, my apologies for that -- that swerve away from questions. We'll quickly turn to some other matters. Because of the translation situation, which is not your fault, we're going to have to move to something else. And I want to ask you some questions about the position as you understood it to be in the villages of Uzdol and Grabovica in that first week or first two weeks of -- of September. Now, in Grabovica, you -- sorry, perhaps I'll -- first of all, you are familiar with the village of Grabovica; correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know where it's situated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. At that time -- we have had in this court sworn evidence that two units of the Bosnian army, one called the Handzar Division and one called Cedo's Wolves, were billeted in huts or buildings on the left-hand side of the village of Grabovica at which location also lived Croatian villagers. Now, my question to you is this: Did you know that at that time there were living and had been living for some time Bosnian soldiers living effectively next door to -- to Croatian -- old Croatian villagers? Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, the fact is that in towns -- or in Jablanica -- I'll take Jablanica as an example. But in Jablanica, there was a multi-ethnic community; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps predominantly Bosniak, but there was a significant Croat presence as well; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in that time --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What does "a significant presence" mean? It's not really specific. What do you mean by "a significant presence"? But there were both Croats and Bosniaks present there. Now, the numbers, that's a different matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And throughout July and into August -- well, perhaps I'll put it another way. In August of 1993, there was a significant flow of refugees into that area from HVO-occupied areas; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Jablanica began to fill up with refugees; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And although you weren't directly involved with the civilian authorities, you knew that the civilian authorities were having a lot of trouble finding places to put these refugees; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And among other people, it was Dr. Safet Cibo who had that job, who was a member of the War Presidency in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wasn't a member of the War Presidency. He was the president of the Presidency of three municipalities: Jablanica, Prozor, and Konjic. So he wasn't a member; he was the most responsible person in the civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly. Now, that flow of refugees did not stop in August but simply continued as prisoners -- as ex-prisoners came across from HVO-controlled territory; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any reliable information about that matter, but probably the answer is yes. Probably so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And certainly from the point of view of accommodating soldiers, you knew yourself that accommodating soldiers became more difficult because refugees were taking up much of the available accommodation in various towns; is that true?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not myself deploy them to these areas in order for me to know that. Probably the circumstances were quite difficult.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a higher-level commander, a corps-level commander, was it your duty to directly supervise the deployment of troops under your command to various huts, houses, or barracks?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the soldiers under my command?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I just mean the soldiers under your command and not to enter into the controversy about who was in command of Neretva 93 at this stage.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But the soldiers of the 6th Corps were not billeted to private homes to share these premises with the civilians. There were barracks or bases where they were billeted. They were not put up in private housing and thus share the housing space with the civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you're aware, aren't you, that Cedo's Wolves were living in the village of Grabovica in September of 1993.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd know it if I hear it from you. I know that they were engaged in the Neretva operation, but I don't know that they were living in Grabovica, because I did not command the Neretva operation nor did I deploy the units, the forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one -- I'm reminded. Could I mark the distributed translation document, one of the three, as MFI145, subject, of course, to what happens at a later time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm afraid not at this stage because we are not going to use this document at this stage. I hope --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As Your Honour pleases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The documents you distributed are just for the reference purpose, you know. And later on - I hope before tomorrow's sitting - that both parties, as well as the court's deputy, could meet together and to reach kind of an agreement which document we are going to proceed on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As the Court pleases. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, your -- the flow of refugees was capable of interfering with or impacting upon military operations; is that correct? And perhaps I'll expand that question. The flow of refugees was relevant to your military operations and you were kept therefore informed about it by your own staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this lay within the jurisdiction of the civilian authorities. They were the ones to take care about the arrival of refugees, their accommodation, food provided to them, so that the corps command had no obligations whatsoever in that respect. What's more, it had its own problems in terms of finding food for the troops, because there were very few staple foods and there was no fuel to prepare them on. We didn't have our own stock to draw upon, and we had to rely on the presidents of the municipalities for food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two -- sorry, perhaps -- could I stop you there for a moment. There's two things I want to raise out of that. The first one is: When troops came in from outside of your zone, they had to be accommodated as and where a place could be found for them; for example, in schools in Jablanica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever premises were available. I cannot confirm now with certainty what these premises were. I only know that we did not have any camping gear, and we could only put them up into the existing facilities or let them sleep outdoors, which would have been the worst possible option, one not to be drawn upon. They had to, therefore, be put up wherever available.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And frankly -- and first, you've mentioned the issue of tents. It wasn't until many years later that the Bosnian army had enough tents to accommodate its troops outside; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was only with the signing of the Dayton Accords and the receipt of donations that it provided with equipment to put its troops into tents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Dayton Accords are in which year?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, this is a weather question. I'm going to ask you whether it was raining on a certain night 12 years ago. But you may recall it because it's the night when Commander Delic came to town in Konjic. And we have the book of Sevko Hodzic and we have statements of other witnesses. So maybe if you cast your mind back to when Delic was in town. Was there a major storm, a major rainstorm on that night and on those days around it, to your memory?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I kindly ask you not to enquire of me such pieces of data. Whoever had any information available about the weather conditions probably had -- relied upon some sources. The month of September is a -- is one with changing weather, and that's true. Now, whether it was raining at the time or not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. The final question for today, and this relates to the village of Uzdol and perhaps to the front line more generally: Was it your intelligence at the 6th Corps at that time that the HVO was planning a large-scale attack on parts of the front line that are depicted on that map next to you, the Operation Neretva 93 map?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that there were certain indications that preparations were underway for a mass-scale attack on the other side, but we did not have any specific intelligence as to when the attack might commence. These were simply assessments based on intelligence pointing to the movement of some forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, those are the questions for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And we are adjourned for today and will meet again 9.00 in the same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 8th day of February, 2005, at 9.00 a.m. 25
